chunks: And regarding the elbow: if it breaks and is set without a defect or flaw, its wergild is one hundred dinars, and that is one-fifth of the wergild of the hand. If it cracks, its wergild is four-fifths of its breaking, being eighty dinars. If the bones are displaced from it, its wergild is one hundred and seventy-five dinars: one hundred for the breaking, fifty for the displacement of the bones, and twenty-five for the exposure. If it was pierced, its wergild is one-quarter of the wergild of its breaking, being twenty-five dinars. If the elbow is bruised and becomes defective, its wergild is one-third of the wergild of the soul, being three hundred and thirty-three dinars and one-third of a dinar. If it was disjointed, its wergild is thirty dinars.
ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for an injured elbow according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage from al-Kafi elaborates on the precise monetary compensation (diyah) for injuries to the elbow joint, distinguishing between simple fractures, displacement of bones, and defects that impair function. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of valuing specific body parts relative to the hand and the soul, reflecting the detailed methodology of early scholars like Shaykh al-Kulayni in categorizing physical damages for legal restitution.
